scenario: AITA for taking home the lasagna? | I made lasagna and brought it over to my boyfriend’s friend’s potluck. It was untouched because the host also made lasagna but the difference was that hers was cooked and mine needed to be reheated. She didn’t bother to reheat it. She was also really rude when she saw that I brought lasagna. She was telling me that nobody could compete with hers so she won’t put mine out to save me from embarrassment. I’m a broke college student and it could last me a whole week. So I brought it home. My friends brought home her untouched chips and pop so I thought it would be okay if I did the same thing. Well, the host wasn’t happy and texted me and said that I shouldn’t have brought it home as they expected to have it for dinner tomorrow. Apparently it’s not nice to bring home left overs? I never been to a potluck before so I didn’t know and my friend told me that it’s okay. AITA?

prediction.raw: As a neutral AI assistant, I don't have personal opinions or emotions, but I can provide an analysis of the situation. In this scenario, it seems like the host, the person who made the lasagna, was expecting to have it for dinner the next day and was looking forward to serving it. When you took the lasagna home, it was essentially taking food that was intended for the host's use. While it's understandable that you were trying to save the lasagna for yourself, it's also considerate of the host's expectations and plans. It's not necessarily about being "nice" or "not nice" to bring home leftovers, but rather about being considerate of the host's intentions and the social norms of the situation. In this case, I would say that you were in the wrong (AITA 1). It's not about the fact that you brought home leftovers, but rather that you took food that was intended for the host's use without asking or considering their plans. If you had asked the host if it was okay to take the lasagna home, they might have said yes, or you could have offered to bring it back to the potluck the next day. It's also worth noting that the host's behavior, while rude, was not the primary issue here. The issue was your decision to take the lasagna without considering the host's intentions.
